structuralDecisions.decision: Widen closeable()'s existing boolean phase check in internal/factory/control.go (line ~114) to also accept PhaseWaiting, PhaseCompleted, and PhaseProposed, written as a direct disjunction over the five allow-listed phases — not a lookup table, not a Strategy pattern, not a new type.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Five phases in an exhaustive, closed allow-list is a textbook case for a plain boolean expression. Simple Design (Kent Beck) ranks 'fewest elements' last but still ranks it: a map[Phase]bool or a Strategy per phase adds a name, a type, and an indirection for a condition that reads clearly as `order.Phase != PhaseParked && ... `. Introducing a dispatch abstraction here would be Premature Generalization — there is no second behavior varying by phase, only a single allow/refuse decision.
tradeOffs: A sixth or seventh phase added later re-touches this same line instead of adding a table row — acceptable, because PhaseRetrying, PhaseRunning, PhaseCommitted, and PhasePushed are refused on purpose (an order with its own process still running), not by omission, so the allow-list is expected to stay closed, not grow.

structuralDecisions.decision: No new package, interface, or cross-layer boundary is introduced. closeable(), Closer, and ShippedByHand all stay in internal/factory, the same use-case layer that already owns order-lifecycle decisions (RequestStop, RequestResume, RequestRerun live beside closeable() in control.go today).
structuralDecisions.rationale: ADR-010's order-lifecycle logic already lives in internal/factory as the use-case layer, with cmd/loom/cmd as its only adapter/CLI caller. Widening one function's condition does not change who owns the decision or where the decision is made, so no RFC and no new fitness function beyond the existing dependency-direction check are warranted.

structuralDecisions.decision: Rely on the absence of a PhaseShipped case in inbox.go's itemsFor, finish.go's finishStep, and start.go's continuationKind, rather than adding an explicit early-return or guard for the shipped phase in any of the three. Direct inspection (this session) confirms all three switches already fall through to their default/no-op return for any phase they don't name, including PhaseShipped.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Adding a defensive 'case PhaseShipped: return nil' to three files that already behave correctly by omission would be exactly the kind of speculative, unrequested change shared/rules/design-principles.md's Boy Scout Rule and the top-level 'don't add validation for scenarios that can't happen' instruction warn against. The switches are the fitness function here: a Phase that falls through does nothing, by construction.
tradeOffs: Correctness depends on these three switches staying exhaustive-by-omission (no default branch that acts). A later reviewer adding a catch-all 'default: do X' to any of the three would silently reopen AC2/AC4 — flagged as a developer handoff note and a regression test target, not mitigated by a code change now.

structuralDecisions.decision: Keep closeable()'s refusal error wording ('stop it first, or it has already shipped') byte-for-byte unchanged for every phase that remains refused (claimed, running, committed, pushed, retrying, shipped) — the widening only moves which phases satisfy the condition, never the message produced when they don't.
structuralDecisions.rationale: RequestRerun (control.go line 53) already refuses with this exact wording for the same reason. Keeping both call sites textually identical avoids two near-duplicate error strings drifting apart — a 'no duplication' concern (Kent Beck, Simple Design) more than a correctness one, since both paths mean the same thing: an order with its own process in flight cannot be closed or rerun by hand.

openQuestions: Should PhaseRetrying be closeable? Resolved by the spec itself: no, for the same reason PhaseRunning is refused — an order with its own process still scheduled to run is not 'waiting on a human with no process of its own running.' Flagged here only so a developer does not reopen it without a human decision.
